sources.citation: Creissels, Denis. 1987-88. Esquisse du système tonal du korokan. Mandenkan 14-15: 81-106.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only the first page read (scan without text layer, not scanned): tonal sketch of Koro, a Manding variety of central Côte d'Ivoire = Glottolog koro1306, not the target language; listed by Glottolog under east2426 refs.

sources.citation: Delafosse, Maurice. 1929. La langue mandingue et ses dialectes (malinké, bambara, dioula). Vol. I: Introduction, grammaire, lexique français-mandingue. Paris: Geuthner. §§439-446, pp. 104-105.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: For generic 'mandingue' (a Malinké-Bambara-Dioula koine): denies lexical tone (§439); 'L'accent tonique, caractérisé en mandingue par la hauteur plus que par l'intensité, et très peu marqué en général, tombe comme en français sur la dernière syllabe du mot' (§441), placement 'soumis à une régularité absolue' (§446). Pre-tonal-analysis; contradicted by all modern work; not specific to Guinean Maninka.

sources.citation: Davydov, A.V. 2017. Manden dialekty Gvinei [Manden dialects of Guinea]. In: Vydrin V.F., Mazurova Ju.V., Kibrik A.A., Markus E.B. (eds.), Jazyki mira: Jazyki mande. St. Petersburg: Nestor-Istorija, pp. 164-171.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Dialectological sketch of Guinean Manden; p.170 describes two basic word tone patterns (H vs L/rising) in Maninka-Mori, tonal inversion in Konya, tonal article; the word 'udarenie' (stress) does not occur anywhere in the chapter.

sources.citation: WALS Online, lects mnk 'Maninka' (east2426) and maw 'Maninka (Western)'; StressTyp2 (local archive StressTyp2-v1-archive-0415).
sources.access_detail: read online, no copy kept
sources.note: No stress features (14A-17A) coded for any Maninka lect; StressTyp2 has only the ISO code row for emk, no entry.

sources.citation: Camara, Mamadou (dir.). 1999. Parlons malinké. Paris: L'Harmattan. pp. 19-22 'Les sons et l'orthographe' (Rosetta Project excerpt rosettaproject_mlq_phon-1).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8491.2.P37 1999); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8491.2 .P37 1999
sources.note: 'Le malinké est une langue à tons. Les deux tons de base haut et bas se combinent.. pour donner un ton modulé montant ou descendant. Mais les tons ne se transcrivent pas!' Guinean varieties (Kankan, Siguiri, Mamou, Dabola, Dinguiraye). Nothing on stress/accent.

sources.citation: Abiven, O. 1906. Dictionnaire français-malinké et malinké-français, précédé d'un abrégé de grammaire malinkée. Conakry: Mission des PP. du Saint-Esprit. (archive.org dictionnairefra00abivgoog)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Pronunciation notes + 'Abrégé' p. IX: only 'l'accent vient en aide pour distinguer les différents sens du même vocable, l'intonation haussant ou baissant sur la même syllabe' (i.e. an early notice of tone). Nothing on stress placement.

sources.citation: Vydrin, Valentin. 2023. Le TAM en maninka de Guinée: la zone du futur. Mandenkan 70; Vydrin, V. 2024. Les adjectifs prédicatifs et les verbes qualitatifs en maninka de Guinée. Mandenkan 71; Vydrin, V. & M. Diané. 2016. L'interrogation en maninka de Guinée. Mandenkan 56: 3-?
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Grammar articles with full tonal notation (tonal article, tonally recessive syllables, interrogative intonation raising register); no statement about word stress.

sources.citation: Vydrin, V.F. 2017. Mande jazyki [Mande languages: family overview]. In: Jazyki mira: Jazyki mande. St. Petersburg: Nestor-Istorija, pp. 16-45.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level statement p.34: 'Stress is absent in most Mande languages; where it can be identified (in particular Bamana) its functional load is small'; foot-level prominence discussed for Bamana only. Not specific to Maninka.

sources.citation: Diané, Mamadi & Valentin Vydrin. 2014. Propositions pour l'orthographe du maninka (Guinée). Mandenkan 52: 3-21.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 3 'Les tons': hundreds of tonal minimal pairs, tone has grammatical role, two major tonal classes (Haut/Bas), tonal article = floating low tone; 'accent' appears only as the name of diacritics. Nothing on word stress.

sources.citation: Vydrin, Valentin & Mamadi Diané. 2014. Segmentnaja fonologija gvinejskogo maninka [Segmental phonology of Guinean Maninka]. In: A. Zheltov (ed.), Antropologija i lingvistika. Materialy peterburgskix ekspedicij v Afriku. St. Petersburg: MAE RAN, pp. 128-144. (halshs-01096618)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Segmental phonology of standard (Maninka-Mori) Maninka; states explicitly that analysis of the tonal system is outside the article's scope, all forms given with lexical tones (fn.3: rising-tone verbs realised low in citation/pre-pausal position). No mention of stress (udarenie).

sources.citation: Vydrin, Valentin. 2014. Ton i akcent v bamana: otsutstvie korreljacii kak teoreticheskij vyzov [Tone and accent in Bamana] (talk, halshs-01076622); Vydrin, V. 2015. Nominalizacija prefiksnyx glagolov v maninka i bamana: razlichija v tonal'nom povedenii (abstract, halshs-01287438).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bamana 'foot stress' argued from iambic vowel reduction; remarks that in closely related Maninka 'the Bamana-type vocalic reduction is absent' (tóló, bòlón, bóló, kóló) and that Maninka's tonal system is close to Bamana's. No positive stress statement for Maninka.

sources.citation: Rovenchak, Andrij. 2011. Phoneme distribution, syllabic structure, and tonal patterns in Nko texts. Mandenkan 47: 77-96.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Statistical study of Maninka N'ko texts (phonemes, syllables, tone marks); 'stress' occurs only in a remark about Latin. Nothing on Maninka stress.

sources.citation: Bird, Charles S. (ed.). 1982 [1981]. The Dialects of Mandekan. Bloomington: Indiana University, African Studies Program. (ERIC ED210934; archive.org micro_IA41153740_0823, scanned text)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kankan Maninka section (p.308-309): vowels do not reduce; tone 'described in considerable detail in Spears (1973)'. General tone chapter notes that in Bambara dialects the last of a series of high-tone words receives a (phrasal) 'stress accent'; for Guinean Maninka refers to Spears. No word-stress rule for Maninka.

sources.citation: Spears, Richard A. 1973. Elementary Maninka-kan. Final report. Evanston: Northwestern University. 256 pp. (ERIC ED091945; archive.org micro_IA41153135_1042)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch.1-2 (pp.1-20): Kankan/Faranah Maninka; course built around H/L tone and tone rules; p.3 'Vowels are not reduced to schwa under light stress', 'a rather complex accentual system' (= tone); p.12 contrasts English stress with Maninka tone. No statement of word-stress position.

sources.note: The only full phonological monograph of Kankan (standard Guinean) Maninka; its suprasegmental chapter is where any explicit statement on accent/stress vs tone would be; cited by Vydrin & Diané 2014 as the most detailed study. RMCA record says printed only (still sold, 12 EUR).
